title: Harness Inspection
summary: A harness only protects you if it is in good condition. OSHA requires inspection before each use, and removal of any system that has caught a fall until a competent person clears it.
talking_points: Inspect personal fall arrest systems before each use for wear, damage and other deterioration, and remove defective components from service (29 CFR 1926.502(d)(21)).

A system or component that has been subjected to impact loading, meaning it arrested a fall, must be removed from service immediately. It cannot be used again until a competent person inspects it and finds it undamaged and suitable for reuse (1926.502(d)(19)).
Body harnesses and components are for employee protection only. Never use them to hoist materials (1926.502(d)(18)).
On a harness, the attachment point sits in the center of your back near shoulder level, or above your head (1926.502(d)(17)).
The system must limit the arresting force to 1,800 pounds with a harness, and be rigged so you cannot free fall more than 6 feet or hit a lower level (1926.502(d)(16)).
The system must bring you to a complete stop with a maximum deceleration distance of 3.5 feet (1926.502(d)(16)(iv)).
The employer must provide for prompt rescue after a fall, or make sure workers can rescue themselves (1926.502(d)(20)).

Good practice (not a quoted OSHA requirement): before you climb, look over the webbing for cuts, fraying, burns and chemical damage, check stitching for pulled threads, and check hardware for cracks, distortion and rust.
site_hazards_to_check: Harness or lanyard with cuts, fraying, burns or damaged stitching
Equipment that has caught a fall and was put back into use
No rescue plan for a suspended worker
Anchorage that cannot support 5,000 pounds per person attached
discussion_questions: What do you check on your harness before every climb?
Who is the competent person who decides whether a system that caught a fall can be reused?
If someone is hanging in a harness, what is our rescue plan and how fast can we carry it out?

flags: Verified 1926.502(d)(15)-(d)(21) verbatim on osha.gov: 1,800 lb harness arrest force, 6 ft free fall, 3.5 ft deceleration, back-center attachment, no hoisting, impact-loaded removal until competent person clears it, prompt rescue, pre-use inspection.
5,000 lb anchorage in hazards list matches (d)(15).
The 'Good practice' inspection point is correctly labeled as not an OSHA quote.
